Subject: Request: high-touch availability commitment for TowerBridge

Hi Logan,

Following our product sync last week, TowerBridge is evaluating Redwood for a core inference path that will serve latency-sensitive pricing traffic. Our leadership has asked whether you can provide a high-touch availability/latency commitment for the initial contract: specifically a dedicated SLA for a small set of endpoints with a p95 latency target of <=120ms for median payloads and 99.95% uptime for the dedicated route.

We understand this is outside your standard hosted SLA — we want to discuss options (pilot, carveout, dedicated capacity) and get a sense of timelines and cost implications so we can move to internal sign-off. Attached is a short RFP with traffic profiles and expected QPS.

Attachments: TowerBridge_RFP_20281001.pdf (pdf, 92 KB)

Thanks,
Alex

Thanks for the ping, Logan. Quick commercial context: TowerBridge is a Tier A prospect (FinTech; late-stage). Expected starting ARR if we land initial term is ~$1.2M, with growth upside. They are very sensitive to latency for the pricing path — this is a conversion driver.

Suggested path from Sales:

I can own commercial terms and run the exec approval if Product/Infra sign off feasibility and Legal drafts the amendment. Can we get feasibility and a rough OPEX delta by EOD Wed?

Appreciate the context. A few product questions before we commit to a target:
- Which model variants and sequence lengths will the pricing path use? 512 tokens? 128? The tail latency is highly dependent on sequence length and KV cache hit rate.
- Is the traffic highly spiky (bursts) or fairly steady QPS? The RFP looks like 350 QPS with short bursts — need clarity on burst duration.
- Do they require streaming responses / function-calling for that route? Streaming increases observed tail latency for certain kernels.

From Product perspective, we can scope a narrow carveout (single endpoint + fixed model version) for a pilot. Requirements to hit p95 ~120ms in practice: dedicated GPU pool (reserved nodes), tuned batching policy with very small latency buckets, and aggressive KV/prefix caching for repeated keys. We also need to define an SLO measurement method (client-observed vs server-side).

If Infra can confirm capacity and a quick cost delta, I can propose an implementation plan and feature gating (route pinning, cache affinity, fallback variant) by Wed.

— Aditya
Staff Product Manager
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: high-touch availability commitment for TowerBridge

Quick infra readout after looking at the RFP and simulating their profile:
- To provide a dedicated route with p95 <=120ms for the payloads listed, we need a small reserved cluster (NVIDIA H100 equiv), with 3 warm standby nodes for failover. That provides redundancy for the 99.95% uptime ask.
- Estimated incremental cost (cloud + reserved infra + observability retention) for pilot: ~$35k/month. This assumes model quantization to bf16 + a tuned kernel set; otherwise cost grows ~20%.
- Operational asks:
  * Route pinning to the dedicated pool (we have a feature flag; will need product sign-off)
  * Instrumentation: server-side p95 + end-to-end client sample collection for 1% of requests to correlate customer-observed latency
  * Runbook and playbook: on-call escalation into Infra SRE team + automatic fallback to a compatible but higher-latency variant if health checks fail

Irene will draft a runbook and estimate lead time: cluster provisioning + config changes = ~3 business days after sign-off. We can run a 2-week pilot.

Irene
Senior Infra Engineer

Subject: TowerBridge — decision & next steps (pilot carveout / draft SLA amendment)

Team / Alex,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Summarizing agreed path and open items:

Decision: We will propose a staged pilot to TowerBridge:
- Scope: single named endpoint (pricing path) pinned to a Dedicated reserved cluster
- Uptime: carveout SLA for that route during pilot period: 99.95% availability (measured server-side)
- Latency target: p95 <= 120ms for the customer's median payloads as described in the RFP (server-side measured with 1% E2E sample correlation)
- Operational controls: dedicated cluster with 3 warm standby nodes, runbook, on-call escalation, automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if health checks fail
- Commercials: Sales proposes the paid pilot (estimated incremental cost for pilot ~$35k/month). Legal to draft a non-credit-first correction plan for first 3 months.

Open items / asks by EOD Wed:
- Aditya: confirm final gating (route pinning + measurement method) so Product can document feature gates.
- Irene: attach runbook + final provisioning ETA (start-of-pilot date).
- Mina / Legal: draft a short amendment (non-binding pilot SLA + correction playbook) and share a first pass.

Alex: we will share a one-page pilot summary and a draft amendment by Thu. If TowerBridge OKs, Infra can stand up the cluster within 3 business days after we sign the pilot amendment.

Attachments: TowerBridge_SLA_Amendment_Draft_v1.docx (placeholder — Legal will update)

Thanks all — action items in HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345 (Marissa please follow).
